title: Git vs GitHub: What's the Difference?
sources: Wikipedia, 'Git' (created by Linus Torvalds in 2005 for Linux kernel development; every computer keeps a local copy of the full repository and history, independent of network access)
GitHub Blog, 'Git turns 20: A Q&A with Linus Torvalds' (first commit April 7, 2005; Torvalds: 'about 10 days until I could use it for the kernel')
Windows Central / SiliconANGLE, Oct 2018: Microsoft completes its $7.5 billion acquisition of GitHub
GitHub Docs, 'About GitHub and Git' (GitHub is a cloud platform that hosts Git repositories so people can collaborate)

lines.text: Are Git and GitHub the same thing?
Git is a free tool that lives on your computer,
lines.caps: *GIT IS | A FREE *TOOL | THAT *LIVES | ON YOUR *COMPUTER

lines.text: and every time you make a commit,
it takes a snapshot of your whole project.
Broke something? Just jump back in time.
And it even works with no internet.
a giant online home where you upload those projects,
so your team can grab the code and work together.
lines.caps: SO YOUR *TEAM | CAN *GRAB | THE *CODE | AND WORK *TOGETHER

lines.text: The wild part? Linus Torvalds built Git
in about ten days, back in two thousand five.
And Microsoft bought GitHub for seven and a half billion dollars.
and GitHub shares it with the world.
